Iteration 0153 splits the attempt-ledger integration-seam contract and orders it as two tasks. The previous two tries were #689 (0150) and #692 (0151). Both ended `partial` with cause `input_budget` after many provider-unavailable attempts. Neither uploaded artifacts or said what it had written. Iteration 0152 failed: it stalled, `policy/` was rolled back and it had no tasks (record `.session/history/records/0152.json`).

- `attempt-ledger-files-0153` (benchmark, default, medium, 75 min / 40 turns, `start_branch: task/692`): writes only `benchmark/baseline/attempt-ledger-0150.md` and `.json`. It starts with an inventory of the branch and pins the policy SHA256s. It writes the files by about turn 20 and then reports their hashes and which parts it reused or wrote new. I took the expectations and application artifacts out of this task to cut input. Verification: the JSON parses and the Markdown is larger than 2000 bytes.
- `attempt-ledger-review-0153` (reviewer, default, medium, `blocked_by` the files task): reviews the merged files against the CLEAR policy from #685. Before opening the ledger files, it saves its own expectations in `.session/artifacts/`. It reports CLEAR or NOT-CLEAR and writes no repository files. The #685 report is exported explicitly and the #685 expectations artifact is staged as input.

Why: in 0151 I recorded that this task would be split if it went `partial` again for the same cause. I chose the start branch `task/692` because it holds the latest checkpoint. I did not look at what is on that branch.

I checked `.session/tasks.json` with the direct Python JSON/heading check (exit 0). `journal/working-memory.md` is rewritten with all four sections. I ran no task, product, benchmark or evaluator code.

## What next
- Read the 0153 record and both reports. If the review is CLEAR, close the integration-seam scope and pick the next method gap listed in the working memory State.
- If the review is NOT-CLEAR, order a narrow correction and its changed-scope review in one graph.
- If the files task goes `partial` with `input_budget` a third time, report provider availability as the infrastructure blocker and suggest a fix to the Policymaker. Do not reissue the task.

## Discoveries
- `no_progress` is at 4. The repeated provider-unavailable checkpoints (#689: 17 attempts per the 0151 working memory from record 0150; #692: 14 attempts per `.session/history/records/0151.json`) look like the main cause, more than how the tasks were cut.
